content: 1. Plasma Levels and Monitoring: When co-administering a CYP2D6 inhibitor with certain drugs, monitor for symptoms of orthostasis and bradycardia. Consider reducing the dose of lofexidine. 2. Lomitapide Interactions: Lopinavir and ritonavir significantly increase lomitapide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Lomitapide can increase ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 3. Lonafarnib Interactions: Both lopinavir and ritonavir increase lonafarnib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Lonafarnib is highly sensitive to CYP3A4 inhibitors, and co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 4. Loperamide Interactions: Ritonavir increases loperamide levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Loratadine Interactions: Ritonavir increases loratadine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Monitor closely. Loratadine can also increase ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1). The clinical significance is unknown. 6. Lorlatinib Interactions: Lorlatinib decreases lopinavir and ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, adjust lorlatinib dosing and monitor closely. 7. Losartan Interactions: Ritonavir increases losartan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Lovastatin Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir significantly increase lovastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, raising the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. Co-administration is contraindicated. 9. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor Interactions: Lopinavir increases lumacaftor/ivacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. When initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the dose initially and adjust after one week. 10. Lurasidone Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir significantly increase lurasidone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Lurbinectedin Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase lurbinectedin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50% if unavoidable. 12. Macimorelin Interactions: Both lopinavir and macimorelin prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is not recommended due to the risk of torsades de pointes. 13. Macitentan Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase macitentan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 14. Maraviroc Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase maraviroc levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce maraviroc dosing to 150 mg BID and monitor closely for toxicity. 15. Marijuana Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase marijuana levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Mavacamten Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir significantly alter mavacamten levels, potentially causing heart failure due to systolic dysfunction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Mavorixafor Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase mavorixafor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor QTc intervals and adjust dosing as needed. 18. Medroxyprogesterone Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase medroxyprogesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 19. Mefloquine Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase mefloquine levels, raising the risk of QTc prolongation and toxicity. Co-administration is not recommended. 20. Meperidine Interactions: Ritonavir increases meperidine metabolism to normeperidine, which can cause CNS toxicity. Monitor closely for signs of toxicity. 21. Mestranol Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase mestranol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 22. Metformin Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir may reduce metformin efficacy due to insulin resistance. Monitor blood glucose levels closely. 23. Methadone Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir alter methadone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 24. Methamphetamine Interactions: Ritonavir increases methamphetamine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Methylprednisolone Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase methylprednisolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 26. Metoclopramide Intranasal Interactions: Ritonavir increases metoclopramide levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended. 27. Metronidazole Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase metronidazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Midazolam Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir significantly increase midazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, prolonging sedation. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 29. Mifepristone Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase mifepristone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit mifepristone dosing to 300 mg/day for Cushing’s syndrome and monitor ECG for QT prolongation. 30. Miglitol Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir may reduce miglitol efficacy due to insulin resistance. Monitor blood glucose levels closely. 31. Mipomersen Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir may increase hepatic enzyme levels when co-administered with mipomersen. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) closely. 32. Mirabegron Interactions: Ritonavir increases mirabegron levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Mirtazapine Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase mirtazapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs due to QTc prolongation risk. 34. Mitotane Interactions: Mitotane decreases ritonavir and lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust dosing as needed. 35. Modafinil Interactions: Ritonavir increases modafinil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 36. Mometasone Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase mometasone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, raising the risk of Cushing’s syndrome or adrenal suppression. Monitor closely. 37. Montelukast Interactions: Ritonavir increases montelukast levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 38. Morphine Interactions: Ritonavir increases morphine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Nafcillin Interactions: Nafcillin decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 40. Naldemedine Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase naldemedine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects. 41. Naloxegol Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir significantly increase naloxegol levels, potentially causing opioid withdrawal symptoms. Co-administration is contraindicated. 42. Nateglinide Interactions: Ritonavir and lopinavir may reduce nateglinide efficacy due to insulin resistance. Monitor blood glucose levels closely. 43. Nebivolol Interactions: Ritonavir increases nebivolol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Nefazodone Interactions: Nefazodone increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Monitor closely. This summary provides a detailed explanation of the drug interactions, emphasizing the mechanisms and clinical implications for each combination.
